newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-BEARDSLEY'S GOALS PUT NEWCASTLE BACK ON TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BEARDSLEY'S GOALS PUT NEWCASTLE BACK ON TOP.

text.p: Newcastle captain Peter Beardsley celebrated his 700th league and cup appearance with two goals in his team's 3-1 derby win over Middlesbrough on Sunday which put them back on top of the English premier league.

Robert Lee added Newcastle's third in the 75th minute as Kevin Keegan's team bounced back from last week's 2-0 defeat at Leicester to leapfrog two points clear of Arsenal, who drew 2-2 at Wimbledon on Saturday, and move four points clear of third-placed Liverpool, who lost 3-0 to Blackburn earlier on Sunday.

Beardsley, who will be 36 in January and who missed a penalty in Tuesday's 4-0 UEFA Cup win over Ferencvaros, opened the scoring from the spot after 41 minutes after David Ginola was brought down by Neil Cox. Beardsley made no mistake this time and and gave goalkeeper Gary Walsh no chance with a blistering shot.

His second goal came after 70 minutes when he shot low past Walsh after being put through by Les Ferdinand. Newcastle wrapped up their win when Lee scored his first goal of the season after 75 minutes with a 20-metre shot which took a deflection off a Middlesbrough defender.
Danish international Mikkel Beck scored a consolation for Middlesbrough two minutes from time as Newcastle ran out easy winners in the 99th Tyne-Tees derby.
